newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican business group against miniumum wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Mexican business group against miniumum wage hike.

text.p: A leading Mexican business group on Friday came out against a rise in the minimum wage during the second half of the year, as proposed by a confederation of labor unions.

"It would be extremely difficult to give an emergency pay raise," Hector Larios, president of the Business Coordinating Council (CCE), told a news conference, saying the added expenses would push many businesses "to the edge of a cliff."

In an agreement worked out among government, labor and business leaders of the Alliance for Economic Growth in December, Mexico raised the minimum wage 17 percent to 26.45 pesos (about $3.35) per day. Consumer price inflation in Mexico was 27.7 percent in 1996.
Larios recognized that the minimum wage still was not enough.
"It's still very low and we should move toward a real minimum wage recovery," he said, but that wage increases should wait until productivity increases and unemployement eases.
Officials with the Work Congress (Congreso de Trabajo) have said in recent days that they will ask President Ernesto Zedillo for an increase in the miniumum wage during the second half of the year.
Miniumum wage increases normally each December following the Alliance meeting.
